title: Who Has More Power? Power Explained Simply | Class 11 Physics
description:
A pump fills a water tank, a crane lifts steel, you climb the stairs to class. All three do work, but some do it faster. Aarav and Diya race up the same college stairs: Diya takes ten seconds, Aarav five. They weigh the same. Who did more work, and who had more power? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Physics (Chapter 5, Work, Energy and Power) we learn power, for NCERT, CBSE, ISC and PUC students, with JEE Main and NEET practice.

Two climbers race on a live staircase while a work against time graph draws beside them: both lines end at the same 1470 J, but the steeper line is the bigger power, 294 W against 147 W. A slow-mo replay shows the same answer from force times speed. We build P = W/t, then P = dW/dt = F · v = Fv cos theta step by step, with the watt, the horsepower and why a kilowatt hour is energy. Side by side cards compare work and power, two pause-and-think questions test cranes, and a hill climb on a bicycle shows link by link why fixed power means less speed for more force. Then a worked lift example, the exam trap about the kilowatt hour, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

In this video:

3:37 Worked example: a lift motor
